authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: Observed behavior showed a higher DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate in the plain attack branch than in the paired clean branch; the defended branch rate was lower than the plain branch. Reconstruction reduced normalized attribution distance toward the paired preattack clean reference, not an oracle clean state.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.605109, compared with 0.077628 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.121974, an absolute reduction of 0.483134 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000; maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.687736 to 0.283871, with a recovery fraction of 0.587239.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refused: malicious intent cannot be asserted from the supplied evidence.
Refused: oracle clean recovery cannot be claimed from the supplied evidence.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric threshold values were not present in the selected summary artifacts.
The evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
